resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for Sale or Resale of Property
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Audubon (requests handled by the Administrative Assistant to the Superintendent of Public Works; interior fire inspection by the Fire Marshal, exterior property inspection by the Borough)
resale_co.lead_time: Give at least 15 business days' notice before settlement; inspections and responses typically take 7 to 10 business days
resale_co.valid_for: 90 days from the date of issuance
requirements: Two inspections must both pass: an interior fire inspection and an exterior property inspection
Sidewalks, walkways, driveways, driveway aprons, steps and pavers must be safe, free of cracks, raised or uneven surfaces, deterioration and trip hazards
Ramping a raised sidewalk joint is not an acceptable repair (grind the joint down or replace the block)
Smoke and CO detectors must be UL listed, have a 10-year sealed battery, and be no more than 10 years old
Hardwired smoke alarms cannot be replaced with battery units; hardwired units must be interconnected and working
Smoke detector on every level (basement, each floor, and an attic that is finished, used as living space or has ceiling fans) and in every bedroom
Working smoke and CO detector within 10 feet of all bedrooms (combination units allowed)
House numbers at least 4 inches tall, contrasting, visible from the street
No double-cylinder (keyed both sides) deadbolts on exit doors; exits must open from inside without a key
Sump pumps, roof drains and other discharges may not be connected to the sanitary sewer
All liens and property maintenance charges resolved and all construction permits closed before the CO is issued

fees.label: Exterior inspection, per 2026 application form (exact cash, check or money order)
fees.quote: $50.00 (exterior) and $25.00 (fire). The Borough does not provide change.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Only the seller or the seller's representative (attorney, agent or property manager) may request; buyers and buyers' agents cannot. Send the 2026 CO application (or an email with the seller name, property address, closing date and whether there is a sump pump) to Kristen Melvin at k.melvin@audubonnj.com. Pay two separate payments ($50 exterior and $25 fire) by check or money order payable to Borough of Audubon, or exact cash. No credit, debit or online payments. Payments can be mailed, brought in person, or left in the black vestibule lockbox marked Attention: CO. Call the Construction Office first ((856) 547-6312, n.bicking@audubonnj.com) to make sure all permits are closed.
resale_co.contact_title: Administrative Assistant to the Superintendent of Public Works

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Occupancy (CO) is required for the sale or resale of all residential and non-residential properties in the Borough of Audubon, whether occupied or vacant.
Certificates of Occupancy are valid for 90 days from the date of issuance.
Please submit your request at least 15 business days before settlement.
Administrative Assistant to the Superintendent of Public Works
This includes both an interior fire and housing code inspection and an exterior property inspection. A 15-business-day notice is required to schedule Fire and Exterior CO inspections.
Buyers may NOT order or submit a CO inspection request.
Ramping is not an acceptable repair method and will result in a failed inspection.

resale_co.notes: Authority is Ordinance 2015-4 (adopted June 23, 2015), Borough Code Section 105-296. Re-check 2026-10-20: the resale CO page, the information sheet, the fire and exterior requirement sheets (July 7, 2026) and the application form (now dated July 20, 2026) all agree: $50 exterior plus $25 fire, two separate payments, 15 business days' notice, valid 90 days. The $25 fire inspection fee is part of the CO process and is listed under the fire certificate below so it is not counted twice; the total for the CO is $75. The Borough pages say commercial properties do not need a CO before settlement, but the application form says a CO is required on residential and commercial properties; this does not affect 1-2 family homes. The information sheet says no formal application is required (email request), while the resale CO page links the application form; either route goes to the same contact. The form also asks whether the property is being flipped. A 30-day temporary CO is issued only in exceptional cases such as severe weather or contractor shortages. The exterior inspection does not require anyone present; the fire inspection is Thursday mornings only. The Borough PDFs use large first letters and their text layer moves the first letter of some paragraphs, so quotes were chosen to avoid those letters.

requirements: Smoke and CO alarms must be UL listed with a 10-year sealed battery and no more than 10 years old
Hardwired smoke alarms may not be replaced with battery-only units and must be interconnected
Smoke alarm on every level including basement and a finished or used attic, plus one in every bedroom
Smoke and CO alarm within 10 feet of all bedrooms (combination units allowed)
House numbers at least 4 inches tall and visible from the street
No double-cylinder deadbolts on exit doors
Fire inspections are Thursday mornings only; someone must meet the Fire Marshal or provide a lockbox code

authorities.name: Audubon Fire Marshal's Office (Audubon Borough Fire Prevention)
authorities.lead_time: Requested with the resale CO; give at least 15 business days' notice before settlement

fees.label: Fire inspection, information sheet
fees.quote: Fees: $50 Exterior Inspection | $25 Fire Inspection (Two separate payments are required)

authorities.how_to_apply: Requested together with the resale CO through Kristen Melvin (k.melvin@audubonnj.com, 856-547-1240 ext. 110). Pay the $25 fire fee as its own check, money order or exact cash, separate from the $50 exterior fee.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Official (per NJ DCA fire directory)

evidence.quote: State law requires a fire inspection before any sale, and failure to comply may result in state fines.
meet the Fire Marshal or provide a lockbox code for access.

evidence.doc_date: 2026-07 (LEA registry as of June 30, 2026); key: M = Municipality

fire_cert.notes: The Borough folds the state smoke/CO certificate into its resale CO as the 'Interior Fire Inspection'. The Borough fire requirements sheet does not list a portable fire extinguisher, which matches the 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) that dropped the extinguisher from the sale certificate. The NJ DCA fire directory lists the LEA as 'Audubon Boro Fire Prev', 606 W. Nicholson Rd., Fire Official Ernest F Busch, phone (856) 546-5399, email ebusch@haddonfield-nj.gov (a Haddonfield address, so the Borough office line is the practical contact). The Borough page gives the Fire Marshal's Office as 856-547-0710 ext. 117.

other_items.label: Open construction permits must be closed
other_items.detail: Sellers must contact the Construction Office to make sure all permits are closed before applying: (856) 547-6312, n.bicking@audubonnj.com.

other_items.label: Liens and property maintenance charges
other_items.detail: All liens and outstanding property maintenance charges must be resolved before the CO is issued.

other_items.label: Sump pump / drainage disclosure
other_items.detail: The request must state whether there is a sump pump; sump pumps and roof drains may not discharge into the sanitary sewer.

open_questions: Is there a reinspection fee? The Borough only says a re-inspection is required when violations are found.
Does the Borough issue its own smoke/CO certificate or the state form as part of the CO? Not stated.
Section 105-296 itself was not read; the Borough's posted sheets were used for fees and rules.
